svg.title: High-Level Dhamma Training: Heedfulness & Skillful Qualities

g.text: High-Level Dhamma Training: Heedfulness & Skillful Qualities
The starting point for practice, driven by the inherent nature of existence
and the desire to end suffering and achieve well-being [7-9].
This motivation drives the individual to embark on the path
Seeking and maintaining connection with those who embody the Dhamma
Associate with Admirable Friends / Teacher / Sangha
Actively receiving well-taught Dhamma, attending to its meaning,
and engaging in discussions to dispel perplexity [15-22].
Listen to the Dhamma & Engage in Discussion
Formal commitment to the discipline of the holy life,
seeing danger in the slightest faults [2, 3, 23, 24].
Core Practice: Cultivating Heedfulness & Skillful Qualities
It involves being attentive, resolute, and guarding the mind from defilements
It is essential for attaining unexcelled freedom from bondage [27].
This involves abstaining from unskillful bodily, verbal,
and mental misconduct, and cultivating their skillful counterparts [37-43].
guarding the doors of the sense faculties
and seeing danger in the slightest fault [44-47].
This involves secluding the mind from sensuality and unskillful qualities
to enter and remain in the
which makes the mind pliant, malleable, and luminous [37, 48-60].
This is the capacity to directly know and see things as they have come to be,
(stress, its origin, cessation, and the path to cessation) [61-71].
It also involves discerning Dependent Co-arising [72, 73]
and the roots of skillful (lack of greed, aversion, delusion)
This is the continuous application of
for the non-arising of unarisen unskillful qualities,
the abandoning of arisen unskillful qualities,
the arising of unarisen skillful qualities,
and the maintenance and development of arisen skillful qualities [15, 76-84].
lack of greed, aversion, and delusion
Cultivate Skillful Qualities & Abandon Unskillful Qualities with Relentless Effort
Through this sustained practice, the mind is cleansed of defilements
becoming luminous, clear, and steady, leading to a state of ease [49, 59, 88-90].
Mind Becomes Purified, Concentrated, & Rightly Released
The mind is liberated from the effluents, and direct knowledge (gnosis)
of the ending of suffering is attained [65, 81, 87, 90-99].
The ultimate goal of the holy life: the complete ending of craving,
the cessation of all stress, and the fulfillment of the task [32, 65, 91, 100-104].
